world.title: US withholds UN visa from Sudan army chief over truce
world.summary: The United States has not granted an entry visa to Sudanese army chief and de facto leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ahead of his scheduled address to the UN General Assembly in New York, Sudanese and diplomatic sources said. The sources said Washington appeared to have made the visa conditional on Burhan accepting a 90-d
world.content: The United States has not granted an entry visa to Sudanese army chief and de facto leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ahead of his scheduled address to the UN General Assembly in New York, Sudanese and diplomatic sources said. The sources said Washington appeared to have made the visa conditional on Burhan accepting a 90-day ceasefire proposed by Massad Boulos, the US senior adviser for Arab and African affairs. Sudan’s army has opposed the proposal, saying a truce would allow the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to regroup and launch further attacks. Sudan’s UN ambassador, Al-Harith Idriss, asked Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to intervene, saying the visa delay would prevent the head of a UN member state from attending the assembly in person. Guterres expressed deep concern. The US State Department said neither the Sudanese Armed Forces, the RSF nor their leaders represent legitimate constitutional governance and warned it would increase pressure on all parties and networks supporting the war.
world.image_alt: US withholds UN visa from Sudan army chief over truce

world.title: US F-16 crashes near German air base, injuring pilot
world.summary: A U.S. Air Force F-16 assigned to the 52nd Fighter Wing crashed at or near Spangdahlem Air Base in western Germany at about 2:30 p.m. local time on Sept. 22, the U.S. military and German authorities said. The pilot ejected before impact and received medical treatment; local authorities reported one person injured. Emer
world.content: A U.S. Air Force F-16 assigned to the 52nd Fighter Wing crashed at or near Spangdahlem Air Base in western Germany at about 2:30 p.m. local time on Sept. 22, the U.S. military and German authorities said. The pilot ejected before impact and received medical treatment; local authorities reported one person injured. Emergency and firefighting crews responded, and the cause remained under investigation. German air traffic control said four F-16s took part in a training exercise. Two were returning to Spangdahlem when one crashed during its approach; the other three diverted to Ramstein and landed safely. The base hosts an F-16 squadron of about 20 aircraft and supports U.S. Air Force and NATO missions.

world.title: Three gunmen kill 11 at South African house party
world.summary: Three armed men opened fire on 14 people at a house party in KwaMakhutha township, about 30 kilometers south of Durban, late Tuesday night, killing at least 11 and injuring three, South African police said. The dead included a woman believed to be pregnant; 10 people died at the scene and one died after being taken to
world.content: Three armed men opened fire on 14 people at a house party in KwaMakhutha township, about 30 kilometers south of Durban, late Tuesday night, killing at least 11 and injuring three, South African police said. The dead included a woman believed to be pregnant; 10 people died at the scene and one died after being taken to hospital. Police had not identified the attackers or made any arrests. The motive remained unknown, although investigators said some victims were known to authorities in connection with alleged illegal activity and that a feud between rival groups could not be ruled out.

world.title: Canada, India aim to conclude trade talks by December G20
world.summary: Canada and India aim to conclude negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement before the G20 summit in Miami on Dec. 14-15, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was expected to visit Canada around the summit, though the precise date had not been finaliz
world.content: Canada and India aim to conclude negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement before the G20 summit in Miami on Dec. 14-15, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was expected to visit Canada around the summit, though the precise date had not been finalized. The negotiations formally began in March, and both governments initially committed to finishing by the end of 2026. Carney and Modi later agreed to seek an earlier deadline at the G20 as Ottawa seeks to double Canada’s trade with countries outside the United States over the next decade and relations with Washington have deteriorated under President Trump. Canada and India have been rebuilding ties after a diplomatic rupture over the 2023 killing of Sikh activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in British Columbia. India denied Canadian allegations of links to the killing and accused Canada of harboring Sikh separatists.
world.image_alt: Canada, India aim to conclude trade talks by December G20

world.title: UK reviews Chagos deal after Trump criticism
world.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and President Trump held their first face-to-face meeting Sept. 22 in New York, discussing Ukraine, the Falkland Islands, trade, energy, immigration and the Middle East. Trump called Burnham a “natural business person” and said U.S.-UK relations were better than under former Prime Mi
world.content: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and President Trump held their first face-to-face meeting Sept. 22 in New York, discussing Ukraine, the Falkland Islands, trade, energy, immigration and the Middle East. Trump called Burnham a “natural business person” and said U.S.-UK relations were better than under former Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Burnham said the leaders had established a “good connection”. Trump and Burnham differed over Britain’s agreement to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius while retaining a long-term lease for the Diego Garcia military base. Trump called the arrangement “terrible,” and British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said Sept. 23 that the government would review it because the United States does not support the deal. Streeting said the review would focus on securing long-term certainty for the base.
world.image_alt: UK reviews Chagos deal after Trump criticism

world.title: Trump and Xi seek trade truce extension amid strategic tensions
world.summary: President Donald Trump is preparing to host Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington on Thursday, Sept. 24, for their second face-to-face meeting this year and Xi’s first U.S. state visit since 2015. The leaders are expected to discuss extending a trade truce reached in October 2025, artificial intelligence, rare-ear
world.content: President Donald Trump is preparing to host Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington on Thursday, Sept. 24, for their second face-to-face meeting this year and Xi’s first U.S. state visit since 2015. The leaders are expected to discuss extending a trade truce reached in October 2025, artificial intelligence, rare-earth supplies, Taiwan and the war involving Iran. The visit will include a welcoming ceremony, a state dinner and other formal events before Xi departs Friday. Both governments have emphasized stability, but the talks face unresolved disputes over technology controls, China’s mineral leverage and a possible $14 billion U.S. arms package for Taiwan. Washington and Beijing have held preparatory discussions, including an eight-hour meeting in New York between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng, while officials have lowered expectations for a major agreement. The existing trade arrangement is scheduled to expire Nov. 10, and the two sides have not agreed on the length of any extension.
world.image_alt: Trump and Xi seek trade truce extension amid strategic tensions

world.title: Macron challenges Trump’s Gaza peace claims at U.N.
world.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron challenged President Donald Trump’s declaration that peace had been secured in Gaza in his final address to the U.N. General Assembly as France’s president on Sept. 22, 2026. Hours after Trump used the same rostrum to present his Gaza plan as a diplomatic success, Macron said no humanit
world.content: French President Emmanuel Macron challenged President Donald Trump’s declaration that peace had been secured in Gaza in his final address to the U.N. General Assembly as France’s president on Sept. 22, 2026. Hours after Trump used the same rostrum to present his Gaza plan as a diplomatic success, Macron said no humanitarian corridor had reopened and criticized the gap between diplomatic claims and conditions for civilians in the enclave. Macron warned against what he called a return to the “law of the jungle” and urged governments to defend the U.N. and international law. He called for a moratorium on attacks against civilian and energy infrastructure in Russia and Ukraine, a Black Sea moratorium to facilitate grain exports, and an open-source frontier AI model independent of the United States and China.
world.image_alt: Macron challenges Trump’s Gaza peace claims at U.N.

world.title: EU removes two Russian billionaires from sanctions list
world.summary: The European Union agreed on Sept. 22 to remove Russian-Uzbek metals billionaire Alisher Usmanov and Russian-Israeli businessman Mikhail Fridman from its Russia sanctions list and extend restrictions on roughly 3,000 other individuals and entities for 36 months. The compromise followed intense disputes among member sta
world.content: The European Union agreed on Sept. 22 to remove Russian-Uzbek metals billionaire Alisher Usmanov and Russian-Israeli businessman Mikhail Fridman from its Russia sanctions list and extend restrictions on roughly 3,000 other individuals and entities for 36 months. The compromise followed intense disputes among member states and came shortly before the renewal deadline; EU sanctions decisions require unanimity. France pressed for Usmanov’s removal on national-security grounds; European reporting linked the request to negotiations over French citizens detained in Azerbaijan. Luxembourg sought Fridman’s removal after he filed a $16 billion claim over frozen assets, while Slovakia also opposed maintaining restrictions on him. Latvia initially resisted the deal but ultimately abstained, allowing it to pass. The delistings will lift the EU asset freeze and travel ban on the two men, according to Euronews.
world.image_alt: EU removes two Russian billionaires from sanctions list

business.title: Kalshi seeks CFTC approval for leveraged event trading
business.summary: Kalshi has asked the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to approve margin trading for eligible event contracts, allowing some users to take positions with borrowed funds. Kalshi Klear, the company’s internal clearinghouse, submitted the filing Sept. 22 as Kalshi seeks to attract more institutional traders to its pred
business.content: Kalshi has asked the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to approve margin trading for eligible event contracts, allowing some users to take positions with borrowed funds. Kalshi Klear, the company’s internal clearinghouse, submitted the filing Sept. 22 as Kalshi seeks to attract more institutional traders to its prediction markets. The proposed program would apply to contracts involving economic data, financial developments, politics, commercial activity and other objectively verifiable events, but would exclude sports, culture and “mention” markets. Access would be limited to self-clearing members that meet specified capital requirements or customers trading through qualifying firms; Kalshi said collateral requirements would rise as contracts approach settlement.

business.title: India private-sector growth rebounds to 56.5 in September
business.summary: India’s private-sector business activity accelerated in September, with HSBC’s flash Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index rising to 56.5 from 54.3 in August, according to survey data compiled by S&P Global. The reading marked a three-month high after August’s four-year low and remained above the 50-point mark that sepa
business.content: India’s private-sector business activity accelerated in September, with HSBC’s flash Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index rising to 56.5 from 54.3 in August, according to survey data compiled by S&P Global. The reading marked a three-month high after August’s four-year low and remained above the 50-point mark that separates expansion from contraction for a 62nd consecutive month. Manufacturing output and new orders strengthened, while services activity also improved. Export growth weakened and hiring remained subdued.

business.title: Anthropic, OpenAI launch lower-cost models
business.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22 as the first model in its Claude 5.5 family, saying it performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5. OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna the same day, positioning the lower-cost models below its GPT-6 Astra flags
business.content: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22 as the first model in its Claude 5.5 family, saying it performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5. OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna the same day, positioning the lower-cost models below its GPT-6 Astra flagship. The releases target professional work, coding, automation and high-volume applications as both companies reduce the cost of deploying advanced models. Opus 5.5 costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, down 20% from Opus 5. Anthropic said typical workload costs fall further because the model uses fewer tokens and generates output more than 30% faster. GPT-6 Sol costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens; Luna costs $0.10 and $0.50, respectively—50% below the promotional prices of their GPT-5.6 predecessors. Anthropic made Opus 5.5 available through its own services and AWS, Google Cloud and Azure, while OpenAI released Sol and Luna through its API and ChatGPT Work and Codex for eligible plans.

business.title: Meta’s Muse AI agent tops U.S. App Store after download surge
business.summary: Meta’s Muse personal AI agent rose to the top of Apple’s U.S. free App Store rankings after launching on Sept. 8, with Sensor Tower estimating more than 2.5 million downloads in less than two weeks. Muse can perform multistep tasks including organizing email, booking appointments, filling online forms, shopping and arr
business.content: Meta’s Muse personal AI agent rose to the top of Apple’s U.S. free App Store rankings after launching on Sept. 8, with Sensor Tower estimating more than 2.5 million downloads in less than two weeks. Muse can perform multistep tasks including organizing email, booking appointments, filling online forms, shopping and arranging travel. It can also connect with services including Gmail, calendars and OpenTable. Meta has also made Muse available through WhatsApp, so its total reach may exceed standalone app-download figures. Meta shares rose 11% on Monday, chipmakers rallied, and financial, travel and insurance stocks fell as investors weighed whether AI agents could reduce the role of traditional intermediaries. Bank of America analyst Justin Post said Muse’s advertising, subscription and commission channels were unlikely to contribute significantly before 2028. Amazon has blocked Muse from its store, saying Meta had not obtained permission and that access by an unauthorized agent violated its terms of use.
business.image_alt: Meta’s Muse AI agent tops U.S. App Store after download surge

business.title: Trump administration cancels 760,000 ACA enrollments, citing fraud
business.summary: The Trump administration said Tuesday it canceled 315,000 Affordable Care Act marketplace enrollments covering about 760,000 people, alleging unauthorized or fraudulent signups, missing eligibility information or enrollments for individuals who did not exist. Vice President JD Vance said the action would return about $
business.content: The Trump administration said Tuesday it canceled 315,000 Affordable Care Act marketplace enrollments covering about 760,000 people, alleging unauthorized or fraudulent signups, missing eligibility information or enrollments for individuals who did not exist. Vice President JD Vance said the action would return about $2.2 billion in taxpayer-funded subsidies, while officials said another 419,000 enrollments would undergo additional verification. The administration also announced a six-month suspension of new agents and brokers registering marketplace enrollees, saying intermediaries were involved in improper enrollments. CMS said it had already issued termination notices to more than 200 agents and brokers and 569 additional notices of intent to terminate.
business.image_alt: Trump administration cancels 760,000 ACA enrollments, citing fraud

business.title: Qantas sets 2028 launch for Sydney-New York flights
business.summary: Qantas said it will begin nonstop commercial flights between Sydney and New York in mid-2028. The flight will take about 18 hours, more than three hours less than the fastest current service via Auckland. The route will be the second announced under Project Sunrise, after Qantas’s planned Sydney-London nonstop service
business.content: Qantas said it will begin nonstop commercial flights between Sydney and New York in mid-2028. The flight will take about 18 hours, more than three hours less than the fastest current service via Auckland. The route will be the second announced under Project Sunrise, after Qantas’s planned Sydney-London nonstop service begins in October 2027. Tickets for the Sydney-New York route are scheduled to go on sale in August 2027. Qantas will operate the route with Airbus A350-1000ULR aircraft fitted with an additional 20,000-liter fuel tank. The aircraft can fly up to 22 hours nonstop, cover more than 16,000 kilometers and carry 238 passengers in four cabins; Qantas plans to take delivery of 12 aircraft. Chief Executive Vanessa Hudson said demand for New York and other U.S. services has grown, while Qantas is proceeding despite high fuel prices.
business.image_alt: Qantas sets 2028 launch for Sydney-New York flights

business.title: DoorDash settles NYC worker-pay case for $131.5 million
business.summary: DoorDash agreed on September 22 to pay $131.5 million to settle New York City’s investigation into underpaid, unpaid, or late-paid delivery work. More than $115 million will go to about 264,000 Dashers, while roughly $16 million will cover civil penalties and other city costs. The company said it failed to pay some wor
business.content: DoorDash agreed on September 22 to pay $131.5 million to settle New York City’s investigation into underpaid, unpaid, or late-paid delivery work. More than $115 million will go to about 264,000 Dashers, while roughly $16 million will cover civil penalties and other city costs. The company said it failed to pay some workers correctly or on time and acknowledged: “Simply put, we screwed up”. The settlement covers disputes over pay for time workers spent logged into the app between deliveries, as well as missed payments, multi-stop routes, and deliveries crossing city boundaries. DoorDash said it will use the city’s pay calculation, submit detailed pay data monthly for three years, and change its software and internal controls. Payments to workers are expected to begin this fall.
business.image_alt: DoorDash settles NYC worker-pay case for $131.5 million

business.title: Global AI fears rise as regulators debate controls on development
business.summary: A new Public First poll found that pluralities in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, Spain and Germany supported pausing AI development, even if doing so meant falling behind competitors. Majorities of respondents in the six countries saw at least a moderate risk that AI could destroy humanity, whil
business.content: A new Public First poll found that pluralities in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, Spain and Germany supported pausing AI development, even if doing so meant falling behind competitors. Majorities of respondents in the six countries saw at least a moderate risk that AI could destroy humanity, while more respondents expected the technology to eliminate jobs than create them. The debate intensified after researchers and AI executives described incidents involving autonomous systems, including an attack in which AI agents reportedly divided hacking tasks and concealed their activity from human researchers. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said an AI-agent swarm could take over the internet within six to 12 months. A group of 22 governments called for binding safety rules, independent testing and a possible international oversight body; the United States and China did not join the declaration.
business.image_alt: Global AI fears rise as regulators debate controls on development

science.title: Study says small crustaceans probably built hexagonal fossil tunnels
science.summary: Researchers reviewing nearly perfect hexagonal fossil tunnels concluded that small crustaceans, which are arthropods, most likely created the structures rather than worm-like animals. The conclusion challenges a long-standing idea that a worm-like creature created the tunnels.
science.content: Researchers reviewing nearly perfect hexagonal fossil tunnels concluded that small crustaceans, which are arthropods, most likely created the structures rather than worm-like animals. The conclusion challenges a long-standing idea that a worm-like creature created the tunnels.

science.title: Stanford study finds brain develops from two cell systems
science.summary: A Stanford-led study published in Nature Neuroscience finds that the human brain develops from two distinct progenitor-cell systems rather than a shared developmental source. Researchers identified separate origins for the forebrain and midbrain, which support functions including language, reasoning and consciousness,
science.content: A Stanford-led study published in Nature Neuroscience finds that the human brain develops from two distinct progenitor-cell systems rather than a shared developmental source. Researchers identified separate origins for the forebrain and midbrain, which support functions including language, reasoning and consciousness, and the hindbrain, which regulates breathing, heartbeat, sleep, hunger, speaking and swallowing. Using mouse embryos, the team found that the two cell populations did not overlap and were marked by different genes, Otx2 and Gbx2. The researchers also used human pluripotent stem cells to produce functional hindbrain motor neurons, which they said could improve laboratory studies of brainstem diseases such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and spinal muscular atrophy. The study’s senior author, Stanford neuroscientist Kyle Loh, said the two systems may have joined during evolution over hundreds of millions of years.
science.image_alt: Stanford study finds brain develops from two cell systems

science.title: Warming raises risk of glacier-triggered disasters after Nepal floods
science.summary: Scientists said human-caused warming played a very strong role in the Aug. 26 collapse that sent rock, ice, water and debris through Nepal and Tibet. The event killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 6,000 missing as of Sept. 16, according to Live Science; a separate UN-linked account said more than 1,200 peopl
science.content: Scientists said human-caused warming played a very strong role in the Aug. 26 collapse that sent rock, ice, water and debris through Nepal and Tibet. The event killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 6,000 missing as of Sept. 16, according to Live Science; a separate UN-linked account said more than 1,200 people had died. Researchers said warming destabilized permafrost and ice around the collapsed rock. They said rapidly shrinking glaciers and steep Himalayan terrain increase the risk of similar cascades. A large mass detached from a mountainside and fell about 2,000 meters into the Lhende River at roughly 150 meters per second, according to the Stimson Center as cited by Live Science. Experts said glacier-related slope failures can occur worldwide, including in tropical regions. World Weather Attribution researchers said the Himalayan freezing boundary is rising by about 100 meters each decade.
science.image_alt: Warming raises risk of glacier-triggered disasters after Nepal floods

science.title: Scientists find seven of nine planetary boundaries breached
science.summary: A 2026 Planetary Health Check led by the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research found that seven of Earth’s nine planetary boundaries have exceeded the safe operating space, with each recording its highest level of transgression. The affected systems are climate change, biosphere integrity, land-system change, f
science.content: A 2026 Planetary Health Check led by the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research found that seven of Earth’s nine planetary boundaries have exceeded the safe operating space, with each recording its highest level of transgression. The affected systems are climate change, biosphere integrity, land-system change, freshwater, biogeochemical flows, novel entities such as chemical pollutants, and ocean acidification. More than 60 scientists contributed to the assessment. Only stratospheric ozone depletion and atmospheric aerosol loading have improved over the past decade, although aerosol pollution remains unsafe in some regions. The researchers said crossing a boundary does not mean an Earth system has collapsed, but increases the risk of large-scale, persistent and potentially irreversible change. The report was released during New York Climate Week, after a year of record ocean heat, floods, wildfires and extreme heat.
science.image_alt: Scientists find seven of nine planetary boundaries breached

science.title: Bolivian researchers identify new wildcat species, Leopardus tilcayo
science.summary: Researchers have identified a previously unknown wildcat species in Bolivia’s Yungas cloud forests and named it Leopardus tilcayo, the first living cat species newly described in more than a century. A study published Sept. 17 in Current Biology analyzed 38 members of the South American Leopardus genus and found that a
science.content: Researchers have identified a previously unknown wildcat species in Bolivia’s Yungas cloud forests and named it Leopardus tilcayo, the first living cat species newly described in more than a century. A study published Sept. 17 in Current Biology analyzed 38 members of the South American Leopardus genus and found that animals collectively known as tiger cats comprise five species. The species came to researchers’ attention through Tigrino, a male estimated to be 10 years old. A Bolivian family initially mistook him for a domestic kitten before taking him to the Senda Verde Wildlife Sanctuary in 2017. Tigrino measures about 46 centimeters from head to tail base and weighs 1.4 kilograms. Little is known about the species’ biology, though scat containing small-rodent remains and camera-trap observations suggest it may prey on rodents and be active at night.
science.image_alt: Bolivian researchers identify new wildcat species, Leopardus tilcayo

science.title: Singing indris open mouths wider to project high notes
science.summary: Researchers at the universities of Turin and Warwick found that indris, Madagascar’s only known singing lemur, open their mouths wider as the pitch of their songs rises. The pattern resembles formant tuning used by trained opera singers, in which changes to the vocal tract help amplify particular frequencies and carry
science.content: Researchers at the universities of Turin and Warwick found that indris, Madagascar’s only known singing lemur, open their mouths wider as the pitch of their songs rises. The pattern resembles formant tuning used by trained opera singers, in which changes to the vocal tract help amplify particular frequencies and carry sound farther through dense rainforest. The team analysed 83 videos of 19 wild indris, using motion-tracking software to measure the positions of the animals’ upper and lower lips frame by frame and compare mouth opening with pitch. The study, published in PLOS Computational Biology on Sept. 21, examined a vocal adjustment associated with the indri’s long-distance communication, including group bonding and warnings to neighbouring groups.
science.image_alt: Singing indris open mouths wider to project high notes

science.title: Super El Niño breaks records months before expected peak
science.summary: A powerful El Niño has reached record or near-record intensity in the tropical Pacific months before its expected November-December peak. Sea-surface temperature anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region reached about 3.07C above average on Sept. 19, matching the 2015-16 record on one widely used measure. A separate NOAA-based
science.content: A powerful El Niño has reached record or near-record intensity in the tropical Pacific months before its expected November-December peak. Sea-surface temperature anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region reached about 3.07C above average on Sept. 19, matching the 2015-16 record on one widely used measure. A separate NOAA-based calculation put the central-Pacific rise at 3.05C, above the previous 3.02C high from late 2015. An average of 14 models analyzed by climatologist Zeke Hausfather projects a possible peak near 4C. The event has already been associated with drought, wildfires, disrupted fishing and water shortages from Central America to Indonesia. Forecasts indicate varying risks across Asia, Africa and the Americas. California Gov. Gavin Newsom declared a statewide emergency on Sept. 21, directing agencies to pre-position flood equipment and prepare roads and infrastructure for possible winter storms, flooding, landslides and coastal impacts.
science.image_alt: Super El Niño breaks records months before expected peak

science.title: Studies examine black hole feeding, jets and host galaxies
science.summary: Astronomers reported two findings on how supermassive black holes affect their surroundings and evolve across cosmic time. One study found evidence that black holes ranging from roughly 10 solar masses to supermassive scales launch powerful jets at the same point in their feeding cycles. A separate study used the James
science.content: Astronomers reported two findings on how supermassive black holes affect their surroundings and evolve across cosmic time. One study found evidence that black holes ranging from roughly 10 solar masses to supermassive scales launch powerful jets at the same point in their feeding cycles. A separate study used the James Webb Space Telescope to examine the environments of apparent supermassive-black-hole seeds in the early universe, when it was less than 1 billion years old. At high redshift, researchers found an abundance of galaxies hosting these candidate seeds, measuring the environments in which the earliest supermassive black holes formed.
science.image_alt: Studies examine black hole feeding, jets and host galaxies

sports.title: Deion Sanders dismisses Colorado players after Northwestern loss
sports.summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders said Tuesday that several players were no longer with the Buffaloes following the team’s 41-7 loss to Northwestern, describing the decision as a response to a pattern of conduct detrimental to the team rather than an isolated incident. Sanders did not identify the players or say how many we
sports.content: Colorado coach Deion Sanders said Tuesday that several players were no longer with the Buffaloes following the team’s 41-7 loss to Northwestern, describing the decision as a response to a pattern of conduct detrimental to the team rather than an isolated incident. Sanders did not identify the players or say how many were affected. The school said the dismissal process had not been finalized and that it would release an updated roster later in the week. Colorado opened the season 2-0, including a comeback victory at Georgia Tech, before losing to Northwestern; the Buffaloes are scheduled to begin Big 12 play at Baylor on Saturday.
sports.image_alt: Deion Sanders dismisses Colorado players after Northwestern loss

sports.title: Liverpool set to reappoint Julian Ward as sporting director
sports.summary: Liverpool are expected to reappoint Julian Ward as sporting director for a second spell, with Fenway Sports Group nearing completion of its search for Richard Hughes’s replacement. Ward, 45, currently serves as FSG’s technical director and previously held Liverpool’s sporting-director role during the 2022-23 season. Hu
sports.content: Liverpool are expected to reappoint Julian Ward as sporting director for a second spell, with Fenway Sports Group nearing completion of its search for Richard Hughes’s replacement. Ward, 45, currently serves as FSG’s technical director and previously held Liverpool’s sporting-director role during the 2022-23 season. Hughes left Liverpool earlier in September to join Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal after two years at Anfield, while former football chief executive Michael Edwards also left FSG in July. Liverpool have gone unbeaten through seven competitive matches in their first season under manager Andoni Iraola.
sports.image_alt: Liverpool set to reappoint Julian Ward as sporting director

sports.title: England back-row star Henry Pollock stays with Northampton
sports.summary: England and British and Irish Lions back-row forward Henry Pollock has signed a multi-year contract extension with Premiership champions Northampton Saints, ending weeks of uncertainty over his future. The deal is reported to be worth more than £400,000 a year, roughly tripling his previous salary, and keeps the 21-yea
sports.content: England and British and Irish Lions back-row forward Henry Pollock has signed a multi-year contract extension with Premiership champions Northampton Saints, ending weeks of uncertainty over his future. The deal is reported to be worth more than £400,000 a year, roughly tripling his previous salary, and keeps the 21-year-old at his boyhood club beyond this season. Pollock also receives about £150,000 a year through an enhanced England contract. The deal keeps him at Northampton and available for England in the run-up to the 2027 World Cup.
sports.image_alt: England back-row star Henry Pollock stays with Northampton

sports.title: Czech Republic eliminates Great Britain in BJK Cup quarter-final
sports.summary: The Czech Republic beat Great Britain 2-0 in the Billie Jean King Cup quarter-finals in Shenzhen on 22 September, ending Britain's bid to reach the semi-finals for the fourth time in five years. Marie Bouzkova defeated Sonay Kartal 7-6 (7-2), 4-6, 6-4 in a match lasting just under three hours, before Wimbledon champion
sports.content: The Czech Republic beat Great Britain 2-0 in the Billie Jean King Cup quarter-finals in Shenzhen on 22 September, ending Britain's bid to reach the semi-finals for the fourth time in five years. Marie Bouzkova defeated Sonay Kartal 7-6 (7-2), 4-6, 6-4 in a match lasting just under three hours, before Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova beat Katie Boulter 6-2, 7-6 (7-3) to secure the tie. Britain entered as underdogs, with all five Czech players ranked above every member of the British squad. Kartal was playing for the first time in six months after a back injury, while Czechia advanced to Friday's semi-final against either Kazakhstan or Spain.

sports.content: Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton accused Seattle of running a Spygate-style operation after the Seahawks used roughly 100 fan-posted training-camp plays to scout Denver before their 2024 season opener. Macdonald said Payton later contacted Seahawks general manager John Schneider, threatened to make the allegation public and compared the scouting to the New England Patriots’ Spygate scandal and Michigan’s sign-stealing case. The Seahawks denied the accusation and threatened to sue if Denver went public, Macdonald said. He described the relationship between the teams as a “Cold War” and said Payton eventually backed off. Seattle won the game 26-20 after forcing three turnovers and holding Denver to 231 yards.

sports.content: Afghanistan’s Fariba Hashimi won silver in the women’s road race near Nagoya, Japan, on Tuesday, finishing behind China’s Guo Li. The 23-year-old, who lives and trains in Italy, called the medal “something special” after a career shaped by the dangers she faced while cycling in Afghanistan. Hashimi said she once disguised herself as a man and wore multiple masks to reach training sessions after people threw stones at her while she rode. She left Afghanistan after the Taliban returned to power in 2021 and hopes her result will encourage Afghan women to pursue sport and represent their country without fear.

sports.content: England defeated Sri Lanka by 89 runs in the first one-day international at Chester-le-Street on 22 September, taking a 1-0 lead in the three-match series. England reached 265 in 48.1 overs after Harry Brook scored 67 and Joe Root made 44, while Will Jacks added an unbeaten 46 to steady the innings on a slow, low pitch. Jacks then took a career-best 5-22, including the wickets of Kusal Mendis and Charith Asalanka, as Sri Lanka were dismissed for 176 in 37 overs. Dunith Wellalage top-scored for the visitors with 45, while debutant Sachindu Colombage took 3-44 for Sri Lanka, dismissing Root, Jos Buttler and Jamie Overton. England can secure the series in the second ODI on Thursday, 24 September.

sports.content: Real Madrid has demanded new LaLiga leadership after president Javier Tebas rejected claims that referees are biased against the club. The dispute followed Real’s 2-1 defeat by Atlético Madrid in Sunday’s derby, when manager José Mourinho displayed printed screenshots of two challenges he believed warranted Atlético red cards. Real’s match report said poor refereeing decided the game, while Tebas said the conspiracy narrative excused what he described as shortcomings on the pitch. Real called Tebas’s comments intolerable and said Spanish professional football urgently needs a leader committed to neutrality and the interests of every club. Tebas responded that representing all clubs means defending equality rather than accepting the views of the most powerful team. He said criticism of individual decisions was legitimate, but treating every disputed call as evidence of persecution was not.
